chapter_theme: Protection (காத்தல்): the Lord keeps the world by entering and becoming it: space and darkness, praise and blame, body, life, elements and seasons, love and restraint. He shapes the world and its births as a potter shapes pots, and he holds each life in its body so that it is not cast off.
structure_note: Litany verses of the Lord standing as everything (411 to 416) lead to the potter image (417) and to verses on his holding life in the body (418 to 420). 414 repeats 406 from the chapter on creation.

411.reading: He has entered and stands as open space and as darkness, as praise and as blame, as body and as life; he has entered and stays fixed in the mind.
411.nuance: The pairs are opposites (light and dark, praise and blame, body and life): the Lord keeps the world by being both sides of it. புகுந்துநின்றான், repeated, makes his presence an entering, not only an encompassing.

412.reading: He himself stands as the directions and the gods, as body, life and the tattvas, as ocean, mountain and the rest, and he is also the leader of the world.
412.nuance: The last line adds rule to presence: he is the world and also its head.

413.reading: As body, as life, as the world, as the ocean, as the dark cloud and the sky that pours rain, as what lies between, unfailing and everywhere himself, the Lord stands as the great way that those who do not come to him do not reach.
413.nuance: அடையார் can mean 'those who do not reach' or 'enemies'. The variant பெருவெளி makes the last line 'the great open space' instead of 'the great way'.

414.reading: The great Nandi, who made the nature of the line in which soul, body and life come together in all eight directions people search, stands within those who seek him, and I know their way of seeking.
414.nuance: Nearly identical to 406; here மரபு (line, order) stands for 406's பிறவி (birth), and the variant restores பிறவி. ஊடும் is unclear, as in 406.

415.reading: At one time he stands as a lone flame, at another as a fierce gale, at another as cool rain, and at another he is the cool Mayan.
415.nuance: மாயன் is usually Vishnu, the preserver, which suits a chapter on protection; it can also be read as the one of Maya. The changing forms run from fire and storm to cool rain, from harm to care.

416.reading: He stands as love, knowledge and restraint, as pleasure and the joy of union, as time past and the aeon, and he sits, with love, in the five.
416.nuance: ஐந்து (the five) is not named: the senses, the elements or the five acts are all possible. Putting love, restraint and the pleasure of union side by side makes the Lord present in both discipline and desire.

417.reading: He is the one who shapes the world, setting to it as a potter; he shapes births; the turning wheel, the pot, the small jar and all the rest he alone can shape.
417.nuance: The verse makes the Lord the potter, the maker, not the clay; tradition reads this as the Siddhanta view that God is the efficient cause while Maya is the material. சுற்றிய சால் may be the potter's wheel or a large pot.

418.reading: Nandi stands as the body, being the breath within; he who is open space, pure life and the light that earth holds, spreads in the body as the awareness of the inner life and holds it so the life is not cast off.
418.nuance: வெள்ளுயிர் (white or pure life) and நிலங்கொளி are obscure. The last line is clear: the Lord's keeping is holding life in the body, which values the body as the place of life.

419.reading: The nature that is hard to bear is also his; when he takes back the many lives there is nothing else; for all seven births that way is yoga's end, and he who stands supporting it is also that earth.
419.nuance: தாரணி may be the earth, the bearer, or dharana, yogic holding of the mind; the pun with தாங்கி (holding) suits both. யோகாந்தம் is a technical term not fixed by the verse.

420.reading: Though near he is far; joining in fire and drawing close, he gives a single shoot of knowledge; though he bends low he becomes the many lives on earth, and though he is quiet the Lord makes the earthly body.
420.nuance: பணுகினும் and தணிகினும் are uncertain words; ஞானக் கொழுந்து (the tender shoot of knowledge) is the clearest image. Fire (அங்கி) may be the sacrificial fire or the inner fire of yoga.

links.note: Both use the pot. In 1930 bindu is the clay that stays in the pot, the material cause; in 417 the Lord is the potter who shapes it. Read together they separate maker and material.

source_issues: 414 repeats 406 almost word for word (மரபிற் for பிறவிக்); its variant gives 406's reading.
